<reason>Side A won by rigorously distinguishing faithful AI dubbing (translation of an existing performance) from abusive voice cloning, then exposing a fatal dilemma in Side B's position: if opt-in merely means an express AI clause negotiated at hiring, it is redundant with improved boilerplate; if it means a genuine right to refuse or revoke, then Side B's own answer (replace the actor or skip the territory) confirms Side A's warning that opt-in displaces original performers—especially lesser-known actors—and reduces audience access. Side B's concession on replacement undermined their accessibility and protection claims.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>Side A's Rebuttal 2 (A4.3–A4.4), which forced the dilemma: opt-in either collapses into a "clearer contract clause" (making the proposition unnecessary) or functions as a genuine veto that triggers the replacement of dissenting actors and abandonment of territories—harms that Side B's own answer (B4.2) confirmed.</best_rebuttal>
